t: There's nothing to see of the church now, but you're standing near where St Peter, Westcheap once stood, at the south-west corner of Wood Street where it opens onto Cheapside. It faced the old Cheapside Cross, and the City waits would play from its roof as great processions went by. It was destroyed in the Great Fire of 1666 and never rebuilt. Sir Martin Lumley, a merchant who was Lord Mayor of London in 1623, was buried here, and he died in 1634.
